examples.title: Industrial Ink service boundary
examples.description: A technical workbench lets a reviewer follow one accepted task through authorization, processing, recovery, and a final human decision.
examples.alt: Dark technical workbench with scenario controls, an accepted task record, and separate cards for request, authorization, transaction, receipt, cache, AI output, disclosure, and decision state.
examples.caption: Figure 1. Industrial Ink gives dense service state a calm hierarchy while one accepted revision remains visible through replay, interruption, rollback, and recovery.

semanticCompanion.summary: The accepted task remains available while each boundary reports its own state and recovery route.
relationships: Interrupt, checkpoint, resume, rollback, or retain the prior accepted revision
A named human accepts a generated claim after its evidence label is visible

examples.title: Soft Color Blocking workflow
examples.description: Broad fields give orientation, comparison, review, and recovery distinct places while labels carry the selected state and the next useful action.
examples.alt: Warm pink and cream workflow with four square state blocks for Orient, Compare, Review, and Recover, followed by selected-state details and a state register.
examples.caption: Figure 2. Soft Color Blocking makes a four-stage workflow approachable while written labels, geometry, and status text preserve its operating meaning.

semanticCompanion.summary: Four written workflow states lead to a selected detail and an explicit next action.
relationships: Review is held with its object and next action visible
Labels, source order, borders, and status text reinforce the color fields
The accepted revision and continuation action stay explicit

examples.title: Component ownership and recovery
examples.description: A review workspace preserves accepted catalog data while a person edits an order, receives a clear authorization result, and recovers from a held or failed request.
examples.alt: Two-panel component workbench with selectable catalog items, a review-order form, request and data status, an accepted receipt, and a disclosure for the semantic state twin.
examples.caption: Figure 3. The component lab keeps accepted data on screen while local intent and authority move through their own validation, failure, and recovery states.

semanticCompanion.summary: Accepted catalog state, local form intent, request state, and authority receipt have distinct owners.
relationships: Catalog revision and item availability remain visible
Email, quantity, and selected item stay editable until submission
Allowed, held, and denied remain explicit states
Prior accepted data remains available when a candidate fails or refreshes

examples.title: Data view, value standing, and evidence
examples.description: A comparison workspace helps a reviewer see weekly case volume, inspect the exact values behind the chart, and understand which values are current, estimated, missing, or restricted.
examples.alt: Data-view workbench with decision controls, a horizontal comparison chart, exact-value table, revision and lineage labels, and a key for six value standings.
examples.caption: Figure 4. The data-view lab keeps the chart and exact-value twin connected to the same accepted records, lineage, units, denominator, and value standing.

semanticCompanion.summary: The selected decision need determines the fitting view while the table and machine twin preserve exact values and standing.
relationships: Compare twelve workflow stages as cases per weekly review
A local two-dimensional chart supports comparison
A paginated table carries the same records, units, and standing
A rejected candidate leaves the prior accepted revision available
